title: MLHSM module manifest
description: One module. The field set extends the manifest MLHSM already has in hsm-core (id, name, description, version, provides, owned_paths, database_tables, route_prefixes, permissions) rather than replacing it, so a module declares the same things to a browser and to the host.

display_name.description: How this installation wants the module called in the dashboard. Absent means the module's own `name` is shown. Presentation only: it must not name a route, grant a permission, or be required for the module to work.

origin.description: Whether the module runs inside the MLHSM process or as a supervised child process. Absent means internal, which is what every manifest written before external modules existed means.

entry.description: How to launch an external module. Meaningless unless origin is external. A registry manifest is untrusted metadata: declaring a command grants nothing - the operator has to install the module locally, and the command is resolved as a bare file name inside the module's own runtime directory.

command.description: Bare executable file name. No path separators, no drive letter, no traversal - the same rule the Rust ModuleEntry::validate applies, so a manifest the registry accepts is a manifest the host can start.

protocol.description: Closed on purpose: an unknown protocol must fail rather than fall through to a default that would be silently wrong.

prefer_arg_port.description: Pass the assigned port as an argument instead of MLHSM_MODULE_PORT. The environment variable is the default because it cannot collide with the module's own argument parsing.

dependencies.description: Hard requirements. A module with an unmet dependency is shown as unavailable, never installed half-way.

optional_dependencies.description: Enhances the module when present. Never blocks installation.

permissions.description: What the module asks for. Displayed to the operator before installation. This phase records the declaration only - the runtime is compiled in, so nothing is granted by this file.

provides.description: Capability labels, shown without loading the module.

owned_paths.description: Paths under data/modules/<id> the module owns. Declaring them keeps a later uninstall from guessing.

database_tables.description: Tables the module owns. Listed so it is visible that disabling does NOT remove them.

route_prefixes.description: API prefixes the module claims. A module may never claim a Core route.

architecture.description: Free-form module shape, e.g. in-process or out-of-process. Kept open so a new runtime does not need a schema change.

artifact.description: The runnable artifact. Absent is valid and means metadata-only in this phase.

permission.description: A capability request. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: an unknown permission fails CI, so a typo cannot silently become a new grant.
